title: Motorsport Branding and Strategic Market Positioning in Saudi Arabia: Infrastructure, Innovation, and Institutional Development under Vision 2030
affiliations: Effat University, Effat University, Effat University, Effat University and Effat University

detail.title: Motorsport Branding and Strategic Market Positioning in Saudi Arabia: Infrastructure, Innovation, and Institutional Development under Vision 2030
detail.abstract: Purpose: Sports has traditionally used as a social activity but today it is taking a new vital role of nation brand building and diplomacy. however, only a few studies have pursued this topic in the recent past. As sports fans become more identified with their respective favorite sporting activities, governments have identified an opportunity to influence the behavior to promote their national agenda. The current study aims at unravelling how mega motorsport events in Saudi Arabia have been leveraged for nation branding and economic diversification efforts. Methodology: The study adopted a mixed-methods design, involving Saudi motorsport stakeholders, including fans. The survey was distributed through online channels, such as university networks and social media platforms relevant to motorsport communities in Saudi Arabia. In addition, structured interviews were conducted. The collected data was analyzed to assess the effectiveness of motorsport events in promoting the Kingdom's brand image, in line with Vision 2030. Findings: The results indicated that motorsport events positively influenced the country's image in the global stage with most respondents indicating that the mega events portrayed the nation as innovative and progressive. These positive sentiments were associated with growing sports tourism and growing sports sponsorships. It also indicates that the sport has promoted the attainment of various targets in the vision 2030 repulsing the sportswashing claims levelled by critics and human right agencies. Value of the study: This study expands the understanding of the economic and reputational ROI of mega sporting events. It would also contribute useful insights on marketers on strategies employable to influence fandom attitude and perception towards an nation or a given brand. management can analyze the importance of sports and fandom and how to leverage this identity can be channeled for the benefit of the brand.

title: Sports Agents Promoting Athletes Internationally: The Role of Technology
affiliations: Fayetteville State University and Fayetteville State University

detail.title: Sports Agents Promoting Athletes Internationally: The Role of Technology
detail.abstract: Professional athletes have been playing their sport in international domains for many years. In addition, every year there are thousands of athletes attempting to achieve the goal of playing in a professional league internationally. Athletes utilize the services of sports agents to secure international contracts. This study explores the factors that play into sport agents getting overseas leagues, companies, and brands interested in their clients. Our research examines whether the technology era provides opportunities for sports agents to successfully promote athletes internationally. We conducted two in-depth interviews with two sports agents. The content of the interviews was systematically analyzed. Five main themes were extracted and further discussed.

title: Brand Loyalty and Global Value Chain: An In-depth Study based on the Integration of Chinese Enterprises and WTO Rules
affiliations: SEGi University, SEGi University Kota Damansara, SEGi University and University of International Business and Economics

detail.title: Brand Loyalty and Global Value Chain: An In-depth Study based on the Integration of Chinese Enterprises and WTO Rules
detail.abstract: Both brand loyalty and Global Value Chain integration could be important factors in strategies for creating competitive positions in highly saturated international markets. This paper aims to assess the impact of brand loyalty on the Global Value Chain integration of Chinese firms under the WTO system. The main research question is to determine what role the Global Value Chain plays in compliance with international trade standards and brand equity in China. This paper uses the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method to map the literature on brand loyalty, GVC integration, and WTO compliance on business practices. This paper notes that enhanced GVC governance enhances customer loyalty by ensuring quality products, and buying firms' satisfaction due to expanded markets. This paper also proposes that observing rules enhances brand reputation by promoting the protection of intellectual property and compliance with international regulations. Finally, the research offers a strategic approach for Chinese enterprises to enhance brand loyalty via culture adaptation, innovation, and services. Practical implications propose that firms need to coordinate global strategies with the local market to be competitive and develop customer loyalty.

title: Polymathy: The Foundational Source of Creativity and Innovation
affiliations: University of Louisville

detail.title: Polymathy: The Foundational Source of Creativity and Innovation
detail.abstract: In an era of mounting complexity and a growing need to transcend siloed thinking, this dissertation advances polymathy as a critical yet underexplored construct in the management and behavioral sciences. Polymathy is framed as an expansive approach to the pursuit, development, and application of knowledge, marked by the conjunction of breadth, depth, and integration. Building on a thought lineage that stretches from Ancient Greece through the Renaissance to the present day, this work shows that polymathy is neither a relic of the past nor an achievement reserved for a few—but a mode of being, thinking, and acting in the world with increasing relevance for today’s challenges. A central contribution is the development and validation of the Polymathic Orientation (PO) Scale, the first psychometrically robust instrument to measure polymathy as a personal disposition—capturing whether individuals value, prefer, and habitually pursue breadth, depth, and integration. The dissertation also advances theorizing through the Developmental Model of Polymathy (DMP), which traces the path from orientation to knowledgebase and creation, and develops twenty propositions linking polymathy to important phenomena, including creativity, innovation, decision-making, and career and leadership preferences. Empirically, the dissertation demonstrates that polymathic orientation predicts creativity across the four stages of the innovation process—idea generation, development, championing, and implementation—beyond the effects of established traits like Openness to Experience. By surfacing both the promise and the challenges of polymathy, this dissertation contributes a more nuanced and multifaceted understanding of human inquiry and its implications for creativity, innovation, leadership, and the flourishing of individuals and organizations.

title: Pathways to Participation: A Behavioural Science Review of Young People’s Engagement in Education, Employment and Training
affiliations: Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University), University of Tasmania - Tasmanian School of Business & Economics and University of Tasmania - Tasmanian School of Business & Economics

detail.title: Pathways to Participation: A Behavioural Science Review of Young People’s Engagement in Education, Employment and Training

declarations.funderStatement: The project was commissioned by Jobs Tasmania, Department of State Growth (Tasmanian Government). The views expressed in this report are the authors’ and do not necessarily reflect those of the Department of State Growth (Tasmanian Government).

detail.abstract: This report reviews the research literature on the drivers of, and interventions influencing, young Tasmanians’ engagement in education, employment and training (EET). It draws on two main sources of evidence: first, relevant empirical findings published in previous policy reports and academic literature; and second, existing behavioural science insights and interventions, applied to the Tasmanian EET context. The purpose of the report is to provide a clear evidence base and practical recommendations to inform policies and programs aimed at improving EET participation among Tasmanian youth.

title: Generative AI-Enabled Empathy and Persuasion in Voice Assistants: Impact on Sustainable Consumer Choice
affiliations: , ETH Zurich, University of Doha for Science & Technology, AI Empathy Research Initiative and Hume AI

detail.title: Generative AI-Enabled Empathy and Persuasion in Voice Assistants: Impact on Sustainable Consumer Choice
detail.abstract: Generative AI voice assistants (VAs) increasingly influence consumer choice. Their empathic and persuasive capabilities offer potential to reduce the intention–behavior gap in sustainable behavior, yet their influence remains underexplored. Across two pre-tests and two main online experiments (N = 1,437; 128.38 conversation hours; 107,842 messages exchanged; over five million emotional expression data points), this research investigates how AI empathy and persuasion affect sustainable choices (meal and delivery) during food ordering. Drawing on the Dual-Action Model, the experiments manipulated AI empathy and persuasion, with cost trade-offs introduced in Study 2. Results show that perceived AI empathy enhances sustainable choice by increasing trust in the AI’s competence, but only when combined with green persuasive messages. Informative appeals are more effective than normative ones in encouraging pro-environmental behavior. Moreover, AI empathy has its strongest effect when the sustainable option is costlier (as opposed to cheaper), acting as a catalyst that helps consumers overcome the personal sacrifice required. We also show that AI persuasion effectiveness depends on consumers’ environmental self-identity, with greater influence on green food choices than on delivery options. These findings offer new insights into the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions shaping sustainable choices in AI-mediated environments.

detail.title: Consumer Climate Contracts

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No personal or financial relationships to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No ethics statement needed -- no empirical studies or participants in studies.
declarations.funderStatement: No specific institutional funding (except some incidental expenses at workshop at Yale Law School).

detail.abstract: This chapter reprises a theory of "climate contracts" in the tradition of social and natural contract theory, with a specific focus on the role that consumers can play in advancing solutions to what scientists have called the climate emergency. Alternative approaches and strategies include consumer-produced climate information, consumer lawsuits, climate-oriented procurement policies, and various kinds of consumer climate cooperatives. Consumer-led actions in private markets can supplement public law approaches to the climate crisis, at least some of which have been slowed or stalled by recent political developments in the world seeking to maintain the status quo and dominance of the fossil-fuel economy. Individuals who act both as consumers making purchases with climate consequences in mind (consumer-citizens) and as citizens lobbying for political and legal changes to make pro-climate consumer decisions easier and more reliable (citizen-consumers) can potentially overcome collective action barriers through organized actions at the scale needed to move the needle toward achieving global climate objectives.

title: Managing Innovation Risk in Package Design with Bayesian AI-Assisted Creation
affiliations: Wisconsin School of Business and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Managing Innovation Risk in Package Design with Bayesian AI-Assisted Creation

declarations.funderStatement: The research was entirely funded by the authors' institution. No external funding was received.

detail.abstract: Package design innovation presents a fundamental tension for brand managers: distinctive atypical designs can capture consumer attention and drive competitive advantage, but also introduce substantial commercial risk by venturing into territories with limited performance data. Traditional predictive models fail in these sparse design regions, providing unreliable predictions and not quantifying well the associated uncertainty critical for managing innovation risk. We address this by developing an integrated framework that combines Bayesian deep learning with generative AI for risk-informed design optimization. Our approach uses a Bayesian neural network to accurately predict sales from product imagery while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. This network then guides a generative diffusion model via a multi-objective loss function to create novel designs that simultaneously optimize predicted sales and atypicality while minimizing uncertainty. Empirical validation using alcoholic spirits packaging shows our Bayesian model is more accurate and better calibrated than traditional networks, especially for atypical designs. Furthermore, in choice experiments, consumers strongly preferred novel designs created with our multi-objective approach over those generated by simpler sales-only optimization or unguided methods. Our framework ultimately enables a more informed navigation of the exploration-exploitation tradeoff inherent in design innovation.

title: Applying Financial Concepts in Project Selection: Insights from Efficient Frontier and Risk/Return Models
affiliations: University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa and University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa

detail.title: Applying Financial Concepts in Project Selection: Insights from Efficient Frontier and Risk/Return Models
detail.abstract: Project selection is a critical determinant of organizational success, yet traditional tools such as Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) often fail to account for uncertainty, interdependencies, and dynamic risk-return trade-offs. In recent years, advanced financial models such as the Efficient Frontier and Risk/Return frameworks have been proposed to improve decision-making, but their adoption and methodological rigor remain uneven. This systematic review aimed to evaluate how Efficient Frontier and Risk/Return Models have been applied in project selection and portfolio optimization, with a particular focus on methodological transparency, model adoption, sectoral and geographical patterns, and integration of emerging technologies. Following PRISMA guidelines, peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 were identified from SCOPUS, ScienceDirect, and ResearchGate. A total of 112 records were retrieved, with 16 studies ultimately included after screening and eligibility assessment. Data extraction covered model type, methodological approach, industry application, geographical context, sensitivity analysis, certainty of evidence, and technological platforms. Journal articles dominated the literature, with increased diversification of publication types after 2020. Efficient Frontier (31%) and mean-variance analysis (23%) were the most frequently applied models, while advanced approaches such as Monte Carlo simulations (6%) and machine learning (4%) were underutilized. Methodological transparency was lacking in 62% of studies, with only 38% fully reporting assumptions, calibration, and evaluation criteria. Geographically, developed countries led in quantitative, model-driven approaches, while developing countries relied heavily on traditional metrics. Sectoral applications varied, with infrastructure and energy projects in developed economies employing advanced models, while ICT and public sector studies in developing regions remained dependent on simpler financial tools. Only 23.2% of studies reported sensitivity or scenario analysis, with Monte Carlo methods producing the most robust outputs. Certainty of evidence was high in 50% of cases but remained moderate (31%) or low (19%) in others, largely due to insufficient methodological clarity. Finally, technological platforms were inconsistently reported; 23.1% integrated cloudbased tools, while 38.5% omitted computational context altogether. Despite growing interest in dynamic financial frameworks, the practical application of Efficient Frontier and Risk/Return Models in project selection remains limited by low methodological transparency, underutilization of sensitivity testing, and insufficient integration of digital platforms. The evidence indicates a need for standardized reporting protocols, broader adoption of stochastic and AI-driven models, and stronger alignment between theoretical rigor and practical applicability. Bridging gaps between developed and developing economies, as well as between traditional and advanced models, is essential for advancing robust, transparent, and equitable project selection practices.

publicationDetails.detailsText: HKU Jockey Club Enterprise Sustainability Global Research Institute Paper No. 2025/134
publicationDetails.journalName: Hong Kong University Business School: HKU Jockey Club Enterprise Sustainability Global Research Institute Paper Series

detail.abstract: Does school spending raise achievement? I show that effects, benchmarked by schools' daily value added, are one-tenth to one-third as large as spending growth. Using school finance reforms for identification, I show that schools did not raise quality measured by value added. Instead, schools raised quantity measured by time diaries of staff and student hours, more than spending, with most hours added after testing. Private time costs of reforms exceed public costs. Achievement effects are small due to fadeout and delayed measurement, suggesting long-run economic effects may be more informative.

title: National Social Investment Programmes Nexus Skill Acquisition Enhancement of Nigerian Youths: A Case Study of Oyo State’s N-Power Beneficiaries
affiliations: Confluence University of Science and Technology, Department of Economics, Faculty of Social Sciences, Kogi State University, Anyigba-Nigeria, Thomas Adewumi University, Confluence University of Science and Technology and Confluence University of Science and Technology

detail.title: National Social Investment Programmes Nexus Skill Acquisition Enhancement of Nigerian Youths: A Case Study of Oyo State’s N-Power Beneficiaries
detail.abstract: The N-power is one of the social empowerment programmes established by President Muhammed Buhari launched on 8th of June, 2016. This programme aimed at tackling unemployment challenges improving skill acquisition in the country. N-Power addresses the challenge of youth unemployment by providing a structure for large-scale and relevant work skills acquisition and development while linking its core and outcomes to fixing inadequate public services and stimulating the larger economy. This study aims to evaluate the significant impact of the National Social Investment Programme on skills acquisition of the youth using N-power programme in Oyo State. From the empirical study, the research design adopted for this study was the survey design. The researcher adopted the purposive sampling technique in selecting sample from the population of study. Sample sizes of one hundred and forty-six respondents were selected for study. The researcher utilized the questionnaire in gathering quantitative data for the study. The chisquare statistical technique is used in testing the hypotheses stated to guide the study. The findings show that the programme has been significant in supporting skills improvement and youth welfare, but not complemented with enough capital that supports business development. It recommends among other things, The N-Power beneficiaries who have been empowered through skill acquisition should be given soft loans to set up their businesses. Thus, the Federal Government should provide interest-free loans to interested volunteers to start up their small or medium-scale enterprises after their vocational training.

detail.abstract:
Objectives. To examine the patterns of cigarette purchasing behaviors and financial burden of cigarette spending among California households following the implementation of California Proposition 56, which increased cigarette excise taxes by $2-per-pack on April 1, 2017.

Methods. Using longitudinal NielsenIQ Consumer Panel data, we identified a cohort of 2,324 California households that participated continuously from 2016 through 2022. The outcomes included cigarette purchasing behaviors and financial burden of cigarette spending. We compared outcomes from the 2016 baseline to each follow-up year and to the 5-year average for 2018–2022 (post-implementation), both overall and by income group.

Results. In 2016, 10.6% of California households purchased cigarettes. This percentage decreased steadily over time to 4.2% in 2022 (p<.001).  However, the reduction over the 5-year period was significantly smaller among low-income households compared to middle-income (2.1% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.004) and high-income groups (2.1% vs. 3.8%, p < .001). Among low-income households, the annual cigarette spending increased significantly from $651 at baseline to $1,053 in 2021 (p=0.043) and $1,343 in 2022 (p = 0.002). Changes in the annual quantity of cigarette packs purchased and proportion of income spent on cigarettes were mostly not statistically significant.

Conclusions. Proposition 56 reduced the percentage of purchasing cigarettes over the 5-year post-implementation period for all income groups, but low-income households benefited the least. Among this group, cigarette spending increased significantly in the fourth and fifth years. Developing targeted cessation programs to help low-income smokers quit could help mitigate the regressivity of cigarette excise taxes.

title: Influence of Chinese Brand Personality on Brand Loyalty Dimensions: An Insight into China's Tea Beverage Brands
affiliations: SEGi University, SEGi University Kota Damansara, SEGi University and Nanchang University

detail.title: Influence of Chinese Brand Personality on Brand Loyalty Dimensions: An Insight into China's Tea Beverage Brands
detail.abstract: The heightened competition in China's beverage industry challenges businesses to maintain market relevance. Industry reports highlight the need for effective brand differentiation, achieved through a distinctive brand personality. While previous research has addressed the link between brand personality and brand loyalty, there is limited insight into how various dimensions of brand loyalty relate to Chinese brand personality structures. This paper addresses two key issues: (1) how dimensions of Chinese brand personality are developed and managed in the beverage industry and (2) the relationships between these dimensions and customer brand loyalty. This study offers valuable insights into the consumer-brand relationship using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design with data collected through mall intercepts and analyzed via SmartPLS 4.0. Findings indicate that various brand personality components affect customer loyalty differently, providing actionable guidance for brand managers and enriching academic and practical understanding of brand management.

title: The Transitivity of Love: A Field Model for Building Communities of Care
affiliations: Arizen Corporation

detail.title: The Transitivity of Love: A Field Model for Building Communities of Care
detail.abstract: Love is transitive" describes a lawful widening of regard: when A loves B, and C authentically participates in B's life or work, some measure of A's care extends to C-not by sentimentality but by structured propagation along real ties. I formalize this as a field model on a social graph with (i) a base relation of regard R, (ii) a participation relation P , (iii) a governance function Ĝ that gates and signs the flow (to prevent halo confusion and harmful spillovers), and (iv) a decay parameter λ that attenuates across distance and time. The model links well-studied mechanisms-evaluative conditioning (affect transfer to neutral stimuli), halo dynamics (trait inferences spreading from a global impression), and emotional contagion-to network-level phenomena like the circulation of social capital and the bridging power of weak ties. I derive practical design moves for "communities of care": how to seed regard where it binds, gate it where it misleads, and instrument it so leaders can cultivate resilient circles without confusing symbols for sources. Testable predictions and ethical guardrails are offered.

title: Cultural Proximity and Housing Investment
affiliations: Zicklin School of Business, Baruch College - The City University of New York, Zicklin School of Business, Baruch College - The City University of New York and

detail.title: Cultural Proximity and Housing Investment
detail.abstract: We examine how cultural proximity shapes major economic decisions, using housing market as the context. Employing Hofstede’s cultural framework, we construct a novel measure of cultural distance between homebuyers and neighborhoods of the purchased properties. Using a comprehensive sample of housing transaction records in New York State between 2011-2021, we examine the effect of culture distance on location choice and transaction price. Buyers are 40% more likely to choose housing units in culturally proximate neighborhood, paying a 1-2% price premium. These results are robust to instrumental variable approach, sample selection corrections and alternative measures of cultural distance.  Mechanism analysis reveals that cultural proximity shapes bargaining behavior: proximate buyers concede more at negotiation, while distant buyers obtain larger discounts. We offer policy implications that effective housing policies must account for the role of cultural preferences to promote more inclusive markets.

title: Climate Strains and the Safety Net
affiliations: Indiana University Maurer School of Law

detail.title: Climate Strains and the Safety Net
detail.abstract:
As the climate crisis deepens, environmental pressures like extreme heat and worsening air quality are steadily degrading daily life in the United States. Distinct from climate shocks like hurricanes or wildfires, these climate strains impact all Americans, but do so unequally, depending on several factors, including people’s geographic location, age, and whether they have the resources to adapt. These climate strains intensify inequalities in education, employment, health, and housing—as the poorest Americans bear the brunt of rising temperatures, declining air quality, and other climate strains.

After defining climate strains and showing their uneven effects on vulnerable populations, the Article critiques federal and state subsidies, investments, and regulations that inadequately address climate strains. It shows how existing programs like the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (“LIHEAP”) remain ill-equipped for the climate crisis due to their block grant funding and outdated focus on cold weather rather than extreme heat. Meanwhile, tax credits largely sidestep poor Americans by making green investments inaccessible to those who need them most. And regulatory efforts to protect households and workers from utility disconnections and workplace hazards have stalled at both the federal and state levels.

To address these problems, this Article proposes a blueprint for reforming welfare programs, tax credits, and regulations to better address climate strains. Its recommendations include prioritizing cooling assistance, providing climate-focused tax credits to low-income households, and strengthening regulations to protect against utility disconnections and unsafe working conditions during extreme weather. This reimagined safety net would more effectively mitigate climate strains, particularly for the poorest Americans, at a time when more and more communities confront the daily strains of a changing climate.

title: Control Systems and Configuration Management in Scope Development: A Systematic Review
affiliations: University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa and University of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, South Africa

detail.title: Control Systems and Configuration Management in Scope Development: A Systematic Review
detail.abstract: Projects of varying sizes often challenge scope creep, misaligned stakeholder expectations, and lack of traceability which can be effectively managed through the execution of control systems and configuration management practices. This systematic literature review examines the effectiveness of control systems and configuration management within project scope development evaluating their impact on managing scope changes, enhancing project alignment and improving overall project performance. Therefore, drawing from a methodologically rigorous analysis of 49 scholarly articles published between 2014 and 2025, the review underlines the evolving role of control systems and configuration management in shaping scope development practices. It reveals a growing emphasis on integrated change control, traceability mechanisms, and automated configuration tools, although notable gaps continue, especially in terms of implementation consistency and resource constraints. The utilization of control systems and configuration management enhances decision-making in scope development and enables project teams to respond more effectively to evolving project requirements. Despite these benefits, many projects face barriers such as system complexity, high setup and maintenance costs, and limited expertise, which hinder their effective adoption and utilization. Our review is based on the analysis of literature on control systems and configuration management. We found 13.48% papers from Scopus, 54.31% from Web of Science and 32.21% from Google Scholar but not all papers were specifically relevant to this systematic review. We advocate targeted educational initiatives, the development of intuitive and cost-effective control and configuration management tools, and strategic collaborations to support knowledge transfer and practical adoption within project teams. Empirical research validating the effectiveness of these practices in enhancing scope control and project outcomes is essential, providing a clear trajectory for future academic exploration and policy development.

title: Stitching Success: Empowering Women Through Skill-Based Entrepreneurship
affiliations: Independent scholars of India

detail.title: Stitching Success: Empowering Women Through Skill-Based Entrepreneurship
detail.abstract: This study explores the transformative impact of stitching and tailoring skill training programs offered to women in low-income communities of Hisar, Haryana. The research investigates how such vocational training empowers women financially, enhances their social confidence, and leads to improved family well-being. Employing qualitative methods including interviews and field observations, the findings demonstrate that these women, once economically dependent, have now turned into self-reliant micro-entrepreneurs. The study advocates for greater investment in localized, skill-based training initiatives and proposes strategic recommendations for scale and sustainability.

title: Doing Things with Political Economy (as a Public International Law Academic)
affiliations: The University of Manchester - School of Law

detail.title: Doing Things with Political Economy (as a Public International Law Academic)
detail.abstract: An increasing number of international law scholars have become drawn in recent years to the study of political economy. In trying to situate the linkage between international law and political economy in its purported historical context, much of this scholarship has tended to construct a vision of a historical relationship between them that typically extends no further back than the 19th century. In contrast, this article situates this relationship in a longue durée with two aims. First, to outline some of the extra-legal factors that installed the historical conditions for a style of international law to emerge that would facilitate ‘public’ administrative capacity and the institutional practices that underwrite forms and processes of contemporary ‘private’ economic life. And second, to experiment with ways that the concept of political economy may be used within international law scholarship.

title: The Birth of Modern International Criminal Law: the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg

detail.title: The Birth of Modern International Criminal Law: the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg
detail.abstract: This chapter provides a basic summary of the International Military Tribunal (IMT) at Nuremberg from 1945 to 1946: procedures that led to its creation, basic descriptions of the individuals and organizations indicted, and a contemplation of the IMT's legacy.

title: Investors' Responses to Market Fluctuations: Evidence from Experiments and Real Tradings
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst, Luohan Academy and University of Oxford, Saïd Business School

detail.title: Investors' Responses to Market Fluctuations: Evidence from Experiments and Real Tradings
detail.abstract: This paper examines how individual investors respond to market price fluctuations, using unique, individual-level transaction data from a trading experiment and the same individuals' real trading history on the Alipay app. We find that, in response to exogenous price movements in the experiment, investors tend to be contrarian traders. Sophisticated investors tend to be more contrarian than less sophisticated ones. We further document that investors' contrarian styles are persistent in the experiment and real transactions. The results imply that investors use simple heuristics from price movements when they make investment decisions in the real world.

title: In the Fed's Mind
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley, University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Berkeley - Haas School of Business

detail.title: In the Fed's Mind
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel text-based methodology to measure the Federal Reserve's real-time attribution of inflation to supply and demand factors. Using large language models (LLMs), we analyze the full corpus of FOMC meeting minutes from 1936 to 2025 in two steps. First, we extract statements citing causes of inflation. Second, we classify each as supply-, demand-, or expectations-driven. This produces a highfrequency panel tracking the Fed's evolving diagnosis of inflation. We find that inflation responds more strongly to supply shocks, while interest rates respond more aggressively to demand-and expectations-driven inflation-an asymmetry consistent with New Keynesian theory but absent from standard Taylor rules. Embedding our measures into an augmented Taylor rule shows that this policy asymmetry becomes especially pronounced in the post-Volcker era. Our approach offers a scalable and transparent method to extract structured economic insights from central bank communication and sheds new light on how the Fed's perceptions influence its policy stance.

title: Regulating Dynamic Contracts
affiliations: CUNY Baruch College and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business - Economics

detail.title: Regulating Dynamic Contracts
detail.abstract: We study optimal regulation of dynamic contracts in a market in which firms and agents meet sequentially, and the firms, who have private information about the match productivity, can offer long-term contracts. Left unregulated, firms use contracts to inefficiently restrict agent movement, and extract all surplus from agents. The regulator can restrict the set of permitted contracts which firms can offer. We derive an optimal regulatory policy in which all contracts take a simple structure, comprising a signing bonus, a flat wage, and a termination fee if the agent wants to leave the relationship. Regulation links the permitted termination fee to the wage, to incentivize firms to offer higher wages to agents with better match productivity, in exchange for more protection from poaching. Our results provide insights into the debate on the regulation of non-compete clauses in employment contracts.

title: Competitive Behavior under Frictions of Trading
affiliations: Universidad Alberto Hurtado and Universidad Alberto Hurtado - Economics Department

detail.title: Competitive Behavior under Frictions of Trading
detail.abstract: Perfectly competitive behavior can occur in individual markets that could not be competitive if only analyzed in isolation from the wider economy: partial equilibrium analysis does not explain competitive behavior. To show that, I study an economy where customers and workers have imperfect access to the firms, and these frictions imply that firms have market power in the labor and product markets. If these frictions are higher in the labor market than in the product market, then the firms behave competitively in the product market by taking prices as given and equating market price with their marginal cost. This occurs because frictions in the labor market prevent the firms from altering supply to the degree required to exploit their market power.

title: Structural Change Detection in Panel-MIDAS-ARDL Time Series Regression Models: An Application to Firm Values and ESG Scores
affiliations: , University of California Santa Barbara, Heriot-Watt University, University of Reading - ICMA Centre and University of Reading - ICMA Centre

detail.title: Structural Change Detection in Panel-MIDAS-ARDL Time Series Regression Models: An Application to Firm Values and ESG Scores
detail.abstract: This paper proposes an innovative change detection methodology for panel MIDAS models, where dependent and independent variables are sampled at different frequencies. Detecting structural changes in mixed-data sampling (MIDAS) models presents a significant challenge for data analysis, particularly in panel data settings. We propose a three-stage procedure for a panel MIDAS estimation. To detect structural breaks, we employ the Cross-Entropy method, which is a fast and precise algorithm. We apply the proposed methodology to a sample of Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) from April 2013 to December 2023. Specifically, we investigate structural changes in the effects of sustainability on the market value of the sampled ETFs. We find that ESG factors have a time-varying effect on Tobin's Q values. This effect is found heterogeneous accross sectors amoung the U.S. ETFs. This highlights the dynamic nature of how sustainability factors are incorporated into market valuations and the importance of accounting for structural breaks.

title: Ahead of Profit Theory: Academic Publishing Running Faster than Science… Seriously?
affiliations: Department of Accounting, Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Sebelas Maret, Surakarta, Indonesia

detail.title: Ahead of Profit Theory: Academic Publishing Running Faster than Science… Seriously?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no financial or personal conflicts of interest related to this study. The only “conflict” encountered was a sense of curiosity almost playful when reading the Scopus 2025 report and discovering that the 2026 issues had already been published in advance. This unexpected finding sparked the reflection that shaped the Ahead-of-Profit Theory (APT). Beyond this mild academic amusement, the study was developed entirely independently, with no influence from publishers, indexing agencies, or commercial stakeholders.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, animals, or sensitive personal data, and therefore did not require formal ethics approval. The analysis was based solely on bibliometric data and scholarly publications accessible in Scopus, including those intriguingly labeled as 2026 issues yet already available to read in 2025 an unusual phenomenon that required reflection but no ethical clearance.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was instead fueled by a late-night curiosity while browsing Scopus reports, stumbling upon the odd reality that 2026 publications were already released in 2025—leaving the authors to wonder whether they were reading science or a trade catalog. In that spirit, the study was carried out independently, without any financial support from publishers, indexers, or other organizations.

detail.abstract: This study explores the paradox of accelerated publishing, where more than 9,200 documents already carry the label "2026" while being indexed during 2025, raising the question: is academic publishing truly advancing science, or merely advancing profit? Using a conceptual review and critical synthesis design, secondary data from scientometric evidence, scholarly literature, and international guidelines (COPE, ICMJE) were analyzed thematically into two strands: supportive studies affirming that management, ethics, and metadata transparency enhance credibility, and critical voices warning that commercialization corrodes trust. Results reveal a striking asymmetry in subject coverage, with technical and high-citation disciplines dominating future-dated outputs, while other areas remain marginal. From this tension emerges the Ahead-of-Profit Theory (APT), integrating four independent variables-publication management, publication ethics, metadata transparency, and commercial orientation-into their collective effect on academic credibility. APT underscores the irony of publishing "faster than science," questioning the reflex assumption that acceleration equals progress. If the trend persists, by 2060, scientific outputs may become so temporally detached that public trust collapses. Meanwhile, publishing remains costly, bound by rigid templating, and often demands LaTeX-style coding-burdens not every discipline is trained to bear. And if authors already shoulder these demands, one must ask: what, then, is the real role of editing-quality assurance or just another gatekeeping ritual? In the end, you too may pause, smile, and quietly ask yourself: is this research a mirror, a mild joke, or simply a playful puzzle left for readers to solve?

title: Presidential Term Limits and Democratic Norm Erosion: An Analysis of Contemporary Challenges to Constitutional Constraints in American Democracy
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Presidential Term Limits and Democratic Norm Erosion: An Analysis of Contemporary Challenges to Constitutional Constraints in American Democracy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was conducted through collaborative interaction with Claude (Anthropos's AI assistant). The human author declares no financial conflicts of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: This theoretical analysis of public discourse and polling data did not require ethics approval as it involves no human subjects research
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: This paper examines contemporary challenges to the Twenty-Second Amendment's presidential term limits within the broader context of democratic norm erosion in the United States. Through analysis of recent political discourse, public opinion data, and theoretical frameworks of democratic backsliding, this study argues that even seemingly impractical challenges to constitutional constraints can contribute to institutional degradation. The research synthesizes literature on democratic norms, constitutional interpretation, and political communication to assess how rhetorical challenges to term limits function within patterns of democratic erosion. Findings suggest that the normalization of anti-constitutional discourse poses risks to democratic institutions independent of immediate practical feasibility.

title: Fairness in Large Matching Markets
affiliations: Tehran Institute for Advanced Studies at Khatam University and Tehran Institute for Advanced Studies at Khatam University

detail.title: Fairness in Large Matching Markets
detail.abstract: We introduce the Truncated Deferred Acceptance (TDA) mechanism, a variation of Deferred Acceptance (DA) that improves fairness while maintaining stability. TDA imposes a truncation level on preference lists of one side of the market before proceeding to the DA mechanism. This truncation of the preference list of acceptors induces competition among proposers, reducing the asymmetry inherent in DA. We theoretically demonstrate that, in a large market with uniform random preferences, setting the truncation level to √ n log n leads to a stable matching in which both proposers and acceptors receive partners of similar average rank.

title: From Cadres to Managers: The Double-hundred Action Programme and China's State-owned Enterprise Reform
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University and The University of Hong Kong - Department of Politics and Public Administration

detail.title: From Cadres to Managers: The Double-hundred Action Programme and China's State-owned Enterprise Reform
detail.abstract: Reforming China's state-owned enterprises (SOEs) is a complex endeavour. Among recent initiatives, the double-hundred action (DHA) programme stands out for its ambition, especially in its aim to revamp corporate governance structures and management systems. A notable change is that top executive positions are now open to a wider and more diverse candidate pool and are no longer restricted to Party cadres. Based on fieldwork and interviews at a DHA-selected enterprise, this paper explores the DHA's impact on SOE functioning and governance. Our research reveals unanimous support among top executives for the policy, despite stringent performance appraisals and limitations on future promotion opportunities. The policy has significantly transformed recruitment, performance evaluation and remuneration within the enterprise under study. However, although top executive recruitment is no longer tied to Party membership, the Party still exerts its influence through key appointments on the board of directors.

title: Performance of the Jibon Bima Corporation of Bangladesh: The State Controlled Life Insurance Corporation of Bangladesh
affiliations: Canadian University of Bangladesh and University of Dhaka

detail.title: Performance of the Jibon Bima Corporation of Bangladesh: The State Controlled Life Insurance Corporation of Bangladesh
detail.abstract: The study attempts to eval.late the performance of Jiban Bima CorPoration (JBC), the only nationalized life insurance company of Bangladesh by analyzing the trend of few selective indicators and fundamentals over a period of twenty years (1979-1998). Although, the analysis of performance of JBC shows a gradual upward trend of various indicators like profits and profitability, value added, Life funds, premium income and income from investment - fundamental analysis reveals that overall profitability of JBC during the years under review is not satisfactory. The poor performance is attributable to the low growth rate of premium,earning compared to the overall growth rate of country's Me insurance business and inadequate rate of return on investment, which is less than the bank rate - a benchmark of minimum interest rate among the overall market interest rates. Reasons of inadequate rate of return are major share of investment are locked in low income bearing term deposits and very small proportion of investment is engaged in shares, debenture and other high income earning securities. So it is evident from the study that performance of JBC can be improved by efficient portfolio management and energizing the policy expanding drive.

title: Exchange Rate Pass-Through, Price Dollarization, and Monetary Policy: The Costa Rican Experience
affiliations: Lehigh University and Central Bank of Costa Rica

detail.title: Exchange Rate Pass-Through, Price Dollarization, and Monetary Policy: The Costa Rican Experience
detail.abstract: We examine whether exchange rate pass-through (ERPT) estimates accurately reflect the exchange rate's role in domestic inflation. In small open economies such as Costa Rica, only a small share of exchange rate fluctuations is attributable to exogenous shocks. Most structural models used to estimate the ERPT effect focus exclusively on these shocks, omitting systematic exchange rate movements that may have substantial effects on prices. We estimate a structural VAR model that identifies inflation's response to all exchange rate variations. A 1 percentage point increase in the annual exchange rate change raises inflation by 0.04 percentage points when driven by an exchange rate shock, but by 0.25 percentage points when the change is systematic. The large gap between these estimates reconciles the puzzle of low ERPT coefficients with the widespread perception that exchange rate movements strongly influence inflation. It also clarifies why the exchange rate, despite its comovement with inflation, is an ineffective instrument for inflation control.

title: Job Satisfaction of Insurance Employees in Bangladesh

detail.title: Job Satisfaction of Insurance Employees in Bangladesh
detail.abstract: Many of us are confused of what Islam says of the concept of Insurance. They hold an opinion that there is no place of Insurance in Islam. For that matter, an attempt has been made to dispel the confusion.This paper examines the existing concepts of Insurance as well as position of Insurance in Islam. It also makes an attempt to make it clear clear that Islam is not against insurance. It has been observed from the study that there are hundreds of thousands of arguments in favor of insurance. In this study, origin of insurance concept and arguments in favor of insurance in Islam are discussed. It is only a humble attempt to highlight the original concept as well as favorable arguments of insurance of Islam.

title: Evaluating CSR Practices in India's Banking Sector: Employees' Concerns and Insights from Factor Analysis
affiliations: Malla Reddy College of Engineering & Technology (MRCET) and Rajah Serfoji Govt. College

detail.title: Evaluating CSR Practices in India's Banking Sector: Employees' Concerns and Insights from Factor Analysis

publicationDetails.detailsText: Suneetha Naisa, V. Suresh Kumar. (2025). Evaluating CSR Practices in India’s Banking Sector: Employees’ Concerns and Insights from Factor Analysis. Journal Of Management (JOM), 12(2), 141-157.

detail.abstract: This study evaluates Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) practices in India's banking sector with a focus on employees' concerns and perceptions. Data were collected from employees of select public and private sector banks through a structured questionnaire, and factor analysis was applied to identify the underlying dimensions of CSR. The results highlighted five key factors shaping CSR practices: community welfare, environmental sustainability, ethical governance, employee welfare, and customer-oriented responsibility. Employees expressed moderate to high concern about CSR, particularly towards initiatives linked to social development and environmental protection. The findings suggest that banks should move beyond compliance-driven CSR and adopt a strategic approach by aligning CSR practices with employee expectations, thereby enhancing organizational trust, corporate image, and sustainable growth.

title: How Stakeholder Influence Shapes Public Sector Environmental Policy Choices
affiliations: Thunderbird School of Global Management, ASU, , National Human Resources Development Institute and Arizona State University

detail.title: How Stakeholder Influence Shapes Public Sector Environmental Policy Choices
detail.abstract: The United Nations Paris Agreement calls for a 45 % reduction in global carbon emissions by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2050. Local governments play a crucial role in meeting these targets by adopting environmental sustainability (ES) policies. However, most research focuses on private-sector organizations, leaving gaps in understanding public sector dynamics. This study examines how stakeholder relations influence public organizations’ adoption of comprehensive versus incremental ES policies and the mechanisms through which stakeholders exert influence. Using the relational view of stakeholder engagement, this research suggests that stakeholder relations shape ES policy adoption through four relational types: communal-sharing, authority-ranking, equality-matching, and market-pricing. It draws on quantitative survey data from sustainability managers in 200 U.S. cities and three sources of archival data using seemingly unrelated logistic regression. The findings reveal that equality-matching relations support comprehensive ES policies, while market-pricing and authority-ranking relations discourage them. Communal-sharing relations support both comprehensive and incremental policies. These findings extend the relational view of stakeholder engagement to the public sector, identifying key stakeholder alliances that can enhance comprehensive ES policy adoption. By understanding these dynamics, public organizations can better align with supportive stakeholders to advance climate goals and contribute to the ambitious targets of the Paris Agreement.

title: Bridging Theory and Practice: A Framework for Industry-Academia Partnerships in Management Education
affiliations: Lincoln University College, Lincoln University College and Rajarata University of Sri Lanka

detail.title: Bridging Theory and Practice: A Framework for Industry-Academia Partnerships in Management Education
detail.abstract: The current study develops and tests a collaborative model of developing management educators' pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) through strategic industry-academia partnerships in the post-pandemic era. Taking a qualitative case study approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews among 15 senior-level educators from Sri Lanka's largest management faculty to explore how collaborative processes bridge the theory-practice gap in outcome-based management education (OBME). We find five main collaborative mechanisms: joint advisory boards, professional development programs, co-teaching arrangements, experiential learning integration, and collaborative assessment practices. Problems of critical implementation as resource constraints, pedagogical inconsistency, and sustainability of partnerships, are revealed through the study, along with how COVID-19 has accelerated hybrid collaboration methods that work around traditional confines. We offer an empirically grounded collaborative model tested against a phased implementation schedule that demonstrates the manner in which formal industry interaction enhances the ability of educators to inculcate relevance while promoting academic rigor. Our model offers actionable suggestions for management education curricula seeking to calibrate curriculum content to evolving industry needs and promote graduate employability performance within developed and emerging markets.

title: Other-versus Self-Referenced Social Impacts of Events: Validating a New Scale
affiliations: , University of Windsor and Tokai University

detail.title: Other-versus Self-Referenced Social Impacts of Events: Validating a New Scale
detail.abstract: Publicly funded sport events are partially justified based on positive social impacts. Past research generally measured social impact for a generic and global "other" with claims such as "Events create new friendships in the community". These other-referenced (OR) social impacts are generally higher pre-event than post-event and are inflated for both methodological and theoretical reasons. In the pre-event period of the Tokyo 2020 Olympic and Paralympic Games, we empirically tested OR items compared to self-referenced (SR) items, such as "Because of the event, I create new friends in the community" and allowed projection bias to vary between scales. Results of the experiment between an OR-Social Impact Scale (OR-SIS) and a similar SR-SIS confirmed OR-measures to be significantly higher than SR-measures. While artificially inflated OR scores may be useful for event organizers and politicians to gain support for hosting, estimates based on circumscribed self (SR) are a methodologically appropriate measurement of social impact.

title: The Uniqueness of Spectator Sport from a Strategic Management Perspective: The Case for Spectatoritis
affiliations: and University of Windsor

detail.title: The Uniqueness of Spectator Sport from a Strategic Management Perspective: The Case for Spectatoritis

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Global Sport Management, volume 6, issue 1, 2021[10.1080/24704067.2019.1641830]

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper uses a strategic management approach to assess the unique structure of the business of spectator sport. We argue there is a lack of business competition because franchises are simultaneous co-producers, collaborators, buyers, and suppliers. Consequently, mainstream strategic management frameworks that rely on competitive environments are ill-equipped to evaluate the nuances of spectator sport. In response to these observations, we develop multiple new and modified frameworks, including a spectator sport supply chain that inextricably links the participatory and spectator sport segments. Through this hierarchy of training, participants evolve from paid customers to inputs to production. Spectator sport and its supply chain are then positioned in the center of a revised industry model to develop a theory of spectatoritis, which is a rational explanation for why spectator sport is not only a natural focus for research, but also furnishes considerable promise for the development of unique sport management theory.

title: The Distinction between Case Study and Case Analysis in Educational and Professional Contexts
affiliations: Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology

detail.title: The Distinction between Case Study and Case Analysis in Educational and Professional Contexts
detail.abstract: The terms Case Study and Case Analysis are often used interchangeably in academic and professional contexts, but they represent distinct methodologies with different objectives in education and decision-making. This paper explores the conceptual and methodological differences between Case Study and Case Analysis, focusing on their definitions, key characteristics, and respective roles in fostering learning and problem-solving. While Case Studies provide detailed, descriptive narratives of real-life or hypothetical scenarios, Case Analyses are structured, evaluative processes aimed at solving the problems or challenges within those scenarios. This article clarifies the unique functions of each approach and demonstrates how they complement each other in academic settings. The paper concludes by emphasizing the significance of both Case Studies and Case Analyses in developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, offering practical recommendations for educators and researchers on how to effectively integrate these methodologies into teaching strategies.

title: The Effect of Unlimiting Bankers' Incentive Pay on Bank's Risk Profile and Value
affiliations: University of Houston - C.T. Bauer College of Business, University of Houston - C.T. Bauer College of Business, University of Houston and University of Houston, C. T. Bauer College of Business

detail.title: The Effect of Unlimiting Bankers' Incentive Pay on Bank's Risk Profile and Value
detail.abstract: How does allowing banks to offer higher incentive compensation affect bank risk and shareholder value? We address this question using UK's recent banker pay deregulation, which removed major restrictions on variable pay imposed earlier by the EU that were binding for UK banks. Contrary to policymakers' fears, UK banks do not experience any increase in tail risk following the pay deregulation, but there is an increase in their systematic risk and leverage. Surprisingly, the pay deregulation does not have a positive effect on UK banks' equity value, which we attribute to intensified labor competition for banker talent. Using hand-collected data, we document a significant increase in the per-person remuneration of senior managers at UK banks, driven by an increase in their variable pay even as fixed pay remains unchanged. This effect is stronger for UK banks that relied more on variable pay prior to the imposition of EU's bonus cap a decade ago, which is consistent with the existence of a persistent bonus culture at some banks. Our findings highlight the unintended labor market effects of regulating bankers' pay.

title:
A Study of Labour Out-Migration in Tea Plantation Sector.

(With Special Reference to Deniyaya, Sri Lanka.)
affiliations: Uva wellassa University of Sri Lanka

detail.title:
A Study of Labour Out-Migration in Tea Plantation Sector.

(With Special Reference to Deniyaya, Sri Lanka.)
detail.abstract: Labour outmigration from the Sri Lankan tea plantation sector has been a persistent trend for decades, posing a critical challenge to the sustainability of this highly labour-intensive industry that relies on a consistent workforce throughout the year. The increasing movement of plantation workers to other sectors in search of improved employment opportunities has contributed to a decline in labour availability, thereby undermining production, export performance, and ultimately, the national economy. This study investigates the factors influencing outmigration decisions among workers in the Deniyaya tea plantation sector. A convenient sample of 175 households was drawn from the estate workforce, and primary data were collected through a structured and pre-tested questionnaire. Probit Regression Analysis was employed to examine the relationship between socioeconomic factors and workers’ migration decisions. The results reveal that educational attainment, social and family status, family size, estate income, and non-farm income significantly affect the decision to migrate, while age and ethnicity exert no substantial influence. Notably, 66% of respondents expressed a willingness to leave the sector, with the majority opting for internal migration to alternative employment avenues. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted interventions to mitigate labour shortages in the tea industry. Sustaining the sector’s contribution to the economy requires policymakers to acknowledge the shifting priorities of the plantation workforce and to formulate adaptive strategies that enhance retention. Recommended measures include the introduction of equitable remuneration policies and comprehensive retention schemes designed to improve worker welfare and job satisfaction. Strengthening such policies is essential to preserving the productivity and long-term viability of the Sri Lankan tea industry.

title: Transforming Accounting & Finance through AI: A Case Study on Google's Intelligent Financial Systems
affiliations: The CVM University

detail.title: Transforming Accounting & Finance through AI: A Case Study on Google's Intelligent Financial Systems

keywords: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting and Finance
Google Vertex AI and Big Query ML

detail.abstract: In today's era of digital innovation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming core business operations, and the fields of accounting and finance are undergoing a major shift. This study examines how Google has integrated AI technologies into its financial systems, significantly enhancing its internal financial infrastructure. Using a detailed case study method, the research focuses on Google's application of advanced AI platforms such as Vertex AI, BigQuery ML, and TensorFlow to improve financial decision-making, automate reporting processes, and strengthen compliance with global regulations. Real-world implementations explored include predictive forecasting, intelligent expense tracking, fraud detection, and alignment with international tax requirements. The findings demonstrate how AI can drive both strategic insight and operational efficiency, positioning Google as a model for modern, AI-enabled corporate finance. This research offers practical frameworks for other organizations aiming to evolve toward intelligent, data-driven financial systems.

title: The Law and Economics of Art. 5(2) DMA: The Case of Meta
affiliations: University of Marburg - School of Business & Economics

detail.title: The Law and Economics of Art. 5(2) DMA: The Case of Meta
detail.abstract: To what extent can Art. 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA) limit effectively the data combination abilities of gatekeepers? Gatekeepers are able to achieve significant data advantages by collecting and combining personal data from various sources. Looking at the example of Meta, it can use the resulting data advantages not only for entrenching further the leading position of its "core platform services" (CPS) but also for strengthening the market position of its remaining products and services. Such data combination practices are therefore limited by Art. 5(2) DMA, unless gatekeepers have presented users with the specific choice and received their consent. The actual functioning of this obligation and its economic effects are, however, still unclear. Thus, this paper discusses the law and economics of Art. 5(2) DMA by focusing on the example of Meta: Despite being in theory able to reduce the data advantages of the gatekeeper, its economic effects will depend crucially on the actual choices of its users. Nevertheless, Meta tries to comply with the obligation by implementing a "consent or pay" model. Any analysis of this obligation needs therefore to consider a legal interplay between Art. 5(2) DMA and the opinion 08/2024 of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), which might make it necessary for firms such as Meta to implement a "third option" in its models. Hence, I propose an analytical framework which considers such a legal interplay and which allows to examine critically compliance questions: While Meta's updated model with three options does still suffer from different compliance weaknesses, the results of a non-compliance investigation of the European Commission (EC) on Meta's initial binary solution can be criticized in particular for a lack of economic arguments. More research that incorporates both the paramount role of consumers as well as the legal interplay is required to prove that Art. 5(2) DMA will be in fact a successful obligation.

title: FOMC In Silico: A Multi-Agent System for Monetary Policy Decision Modeling
affiliations: Stanford University and George Washington University - Department of Economics

detail.title: FOMC In Silico: A Multi-Agent System for Monetary Policy Decision Modeling
detail.abstract: We develop a multi-agent framework for modeling the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision making process. The framework combines two approaches: an LLM-based simulation and a Monte Carlo implementation of a generalized Bayesian voting model. Both begin from identical prior beliefs about the appropriate interest rate for each committee member, formed using real-time data and member profiles. In a simulation replicating the July 2025 FOMC meeting, both tracks deliver rates near the 4.25-4.50% range's upper end (4.42% LLM, 4.38% MC). Political pressure scenario increases dissent and dispersion: the LLM track averages 4.38% and shows dissent in 88% of meetings; the MC track averages 4.39% and shows dissent in 61% of meetings. A negative jobs revision scenario moves outcomes lower: LLM at 4.30% (dissent in 74% of meeting), and MC at 4.32% (dissent in 62% of meeting), with final decisions remaining inside the 4.25-4.50% range. The framework isolates small, scenario-dependent wedges between behavioral and rational baselines, offering an in silico environment for counterfactual evaluation in monetary policy.

title:
Lebanon's Maritime Identity: From Tragedy to Renewal 
Inspired by Loss, Anchored in Possibility
affiliations: Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK)

detail.title:
Lebanon's Maritime Identity: From Tragedy to Renewal 
Inspired by Loss, Anchored in Possibility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This essay reflects on Lebanon’s maritime identity at the intersection of national tragedy and global development. Marking the fifth anniversary of the Beirut Port explosion (August 4, 2020) and the United Nations’ Third Conference on Landlocked Developing Countries (LLDC3) in August 2025, it situates Lebanon’s 200+ km Mediterranean coastline as both a site of mourning and a reservoir of untapped potential. While regional rivals invest in digitalized, AI-enabled, and ecologically adaptive mega-ports, Lebanon continues to suffer from governance failures rather than geographic constraints. Against this backdrop, the article proposes a vision for a Lebanese maritime renaissance rooted in Phoenician principles of connectivity, specialization, and trade networks. It explores innovative pathways such as “sea-to-summit” logistics, decentralized blue economy models, diaspora-led investment partnerships, and port-based cultural industries. The essay argues that Lebanon’s ports can evolve into hubs of sustainability, heritage, and innovation, positioning the country within Euro-Mediterranean networks while providing local jobs, fostering tourism, and engaging its global diaspora. Ultimately, Lebanon’s maritime future lies not in competing with regional mega-projects but in embracing an agile, distributed, story-rich approach where prosperity flows through both commerce and culture, transforming a legacy of loss into a vision of renewal.

title: Decarbonizing the U.S. Aluminum Ecosystem using a Dynamic Material Flow Simulation Framework
affiliations: Binghamton University, Argonne National Laboratory, University of Michigan and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: Decarbonizing the U.S. Aluminum Ecosystem using a Dynamic Material Flow Simulation Framework
detail.abstract: Aluminum is vital to clean energy industries but a major source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, necessitating supply chain decarbonization. Achieving this requires insight into material flows and interactions between decarbonization pathways. This study holistically analyzes the U.S. aluminum supply chain and its GHG emissions through system modeling and simulation. An object-oriented system model is developed to digitally represent the U.S. aluminum supply chain, enabling simulation of consumption-driven material flows and GHG emissions from both domestic production and imported feedstocks. A range of decarbonization pathways was applied to U.S. domestic activities and evaluated over 2020–2050. To assess interactions and combined impacts under uncertainty, strategy portfolios were modeled using a design of experiments framework with stochastic demand simulation. The most effective single pathway for reducing total emissions is improving process yields, as it significantly lowers import demand—though it can diminish the benefits of other measures like reducing process emissions. In contrast, pathways like electrification and grid decarbonization are synergistic. For domestic emissions alone, the most impactful measure is switching from natural gas to clean hydrogen. However, both hydrogen switching and process electrification may increase emissions unless the hydrogen supply and electricity grid are also decarbonized. A strategy combining multiple decarbonization pathways—including grid decarbonization, electrification of process heat, adoption of inert anodes in primary production, and increased domestic recycling of post-consumer scrap—could reduce annual GHG emissions from the U.S. domestic aluminum supply chain by 91.5% (34% when accounting for imports) by 2050 relative to 2020.

title: Domestic Money Pools as Operator Being, Excitations, and the Infrastructure Question
affiliations: University of Birmingham

detail.title: Domestic Money Pools as Operator Being, Excitations, and the Infrastructure Question

declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A

detail.abstract: Africa’s infrastructure debate has been dominated by financing gaps and project pipelines. Yet numbers alone conceal the deeper truth: infrastructure is a far-from-equilibrium event, embedded in the complexity of state, market, and society. This paper reframes the question through the lens of domestic money pools (DMPs). At their ground state (World 0), DMPs are not mere liquidity but operators of trust - a justification of Being. They encounter excitations in World 1, producing perturbations that demand narratives in World 2, often reduced to the shorthand of bankability. In World 3, instruments such as credit scoring further reshape meaning, narrowing or widening the operator. Drawing on the Four Worlds and the Layered Operator Appraisal frameworks, the paper develops an operator-theoretic view of DMPs, with kernels that condition long-tailed transformations. Takeaway: the state of the domestic money pool is itself the measure of Africa’s infrastructure future.

title: Tambora Eruption and Peasant Revolts in Ancient China: An Apocalypse
affiliations: Nanjing University - Department of Economics, Fudan University - Department of Economics and Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE)

detail.title: Tambora Eruption and Peasant Revolts in Ancient China: An Apocalypse
detail.abstract: The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the deadliest volcanic eruption in recorded human history. Massive amounts of toxic chemicals were ejected into the atmosphere, blocking solar radiation and triggering global temperature declines. We leverage this unique natural experiment to examine two channels through which climate disasters impact social stability. Using novel prefecturelevel data from the Qing Dynasty of China, we find a one-standard-deviation increase a prefecture's solar heat requirement for crop growth witnessed a 18.8% increase in peasant revolts. Consistent with the widely-recognized food shortage channel, we show the cooling-induced crop failure boosted crop prices which induced social instability. Notably, we show evdience supporting a belief channel that has been overlooked by economics literature. The Tambora-affected regions witnessed significant uprisings of the White Lotus, the largest millenarian religion inciting peasant revolts against the Qing emperor. Our findings are robust to alternative specifications, economic conditions, and social events.

title: Harvesting Votes: The Electoral Effects of the Italian Land Reform
affiliations: University of St Gallen, University of Zurich and University of Zurich - Department of Economics

detail.title: Harvesting Votes: The Electoral Effects of the Italian Land Reform
detail.abstract: Governments often implement large-scale redistribution policies to gain enduring political support. However, little is known on whether such policies generate sizable gains, whether these gains are persistent, and why. We study the political consequences of a major land reform in Italy. In a sample of towns close to the reform border, difference-indifferences estimates show that the reform generated large electoral gains for the incumbent Christian Democratic party. The electoral effects persist over four decades. We show that the reform initiated a sustained exchange between voters and politicians, rooted in clientelistic brokering and political patronage, which helped the Christian Democrats maintain the initial gains. We also examine alternative explanations-such as economic development, structural transformation, and shifts in political attitudes-but find little consistent evidence to support these channels.

title: Place-Based Variation in Health Care: Evidence from Mandatory Movers in the U.S. Military Health System
affiliations: Institute for Defense Analyses, Institute for Defense Analyses, Institute for Defense Analyses and Dartmouth College - Department of Economics

detail.title: Place-Based Variation in Health Care: Evidence from Mandatory Movers in the U.S. Military Health System

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
There is increasing evidence on regional variations in U.S. Medicare utilization based on older patients who move. Yet evidence is limited for younger ages in the U.S., and movers may differ systematically from those who don’t move. In this paper, we harness the mandatory migration of military personnel and dependents (age 5 to 64) to estimate supply and demand factors in a system of care in which military physicians are salaried and copayments and deductibles are negligible. In our sample of 3 million enrollees, we find that place or supply effects explain as much as 80 percent of the overall regional variation for both the entire sample and for active-duty personnel. These regional place effects are correlated across age groups, with correlations as high as 0.84 between middle-aged and older military enrollees. These regional supply-side variations cannot be explained by differences in health, financial incentives, or quality of care, but appear consistent with location-specific differences in physician beliefs.

Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Jump Detection in Financial Asset Prices that Exhibit U-Shape Volatility
affiliations: University of Verona - Department of Economics

detail.title: Jump Detection in Financial Asset Prices that Exhibit U-Shape Volatility
detail.abstract: We describe a Matlab routine that allows us to estimate the jumps in financial asset prices using the Threshold (or Truncation) method of [Man09]. The routine is designed for application to five-minute log-returns, for which microstructure noises are commonly considered negligible. The underlying assumption is that asset prices evolve in time following an Ito semimartingale with, possibly stochastic, volatility and jumps. A log-return is likely to contain a jump if its absolute value is larger than a threshold determined by the maximum increment of the Brownian semimartingale (BS) part. The increments of a BS are particularly sensitive to the magnitude of the volatility coeƯicient, and from an empirical point of view, volatility levels typically depend on the time of day (TOD), with volatility being highest at the beginning and end of the day, while it is low in the middle. The first routine presented allows for an estimation of the TOD eƯect, and is an implementation of the method described in [BolTod2011], appendix B. Subsequently, the routine is used to visualize the TOD eƯect for the stock Apple Inc. (AAPL). The second routine presented is an implementation of the threshold method for estimating jumps in AAPL prices. The procedure begins with the construction of a first-round threshold obtained using an initial raw estimate baralpha of the average daily volatility level, and the diƯerent TOD factors for the diƯerent times of the day.
